input: The retrofit capital should not be committed on the present evidence. Instead, a metered trial on one refrigeration line should come first, with the plant engineer owning the trial, and the capital decision should follow once the trial result is available. By way of background, the plant uses 2217 MWh of electricity per year in refrigeration, and refrigeration is the load that the retrofit addresses. The vendor projects a saving of 17% of that use, which corresponds to a derived saving of 377 MWh per year at the vendor figure, and the saving is valued at an electricity price of $0.1 per kWh. A derived annual saving of $38k set against a capital cost of $509k gives a derived simple payback of 13.4 years. It must be emphasised, however, that every saving figure in the case is the vendor's projection: none of it was measured at this plant, and the refrigeration load in the summer peak month was not modelled, so the projection remains untested at the plant and untested in the month when the refrigeration load is at its highest. A metered trial on one of the three refrigeration lines would measure the saving on the plant's own load, in the plant's own operating pattern, before any capital is committed. Metering one line also fixes the measurement method, so that the trial figure and the vendor figure stand on the same basis when they are compared.
